AgencyInvitationPreview.description: What an unauthenticated visitor sees before deciding to log in and accept.
AgencyInvitationPreview.title: AgencyInvitationPreview

AgencyProfileRead.description:
The general agency profile — branding, about/contact, socials, policies.
Storage paths for the images are never exposed; the frontend fetches the
bytes through GET /agencies/{id}/logo (proxied).
AgencyProfileRead.title: AgencyProfileRead

BoardItemUpdate.description:
Every field optional — the canvas PATCHes just what changed (a drag
sends x/y, a resize sends width/height, an edit sends content).
BoardItemUpdate.title: BoardItemUpdate

ClientBrandingRead.description:
A client's own portal branding — colors, welcome message, and whether
a logo is set. Storage paths are never exposed; the frontend fetches the
logo's bytes through GET .../branding/logo (staff) or GET /portal/logo
(the client's own portal), same rule as AgencyProfileRead.
ClientBrandingRead.title: ClientBrandingRead

ClientInvitationPreview.description: What an unauthenticated visitor sees before logging in to accept.
ClientInvitationPreview.title: ClientInvitationPreview

DashboardRead.description:
One-shot aggregate for the Overview tab — replaces what used to be 7
separate agency-scoped requests (projects, clients, invoice summary,
overdue invoices, activity, unread count, my work) with a single call.
DashboardRead.title: DashboardRead

InvoiceParty.description: The 'from' (agency) or 'bill to' (client) block on a rendered invoice.
InvoiceParty.title: InvoiceParty

InvoiceUpdate.description: Full replace of a draft invoice — same shape as create.
InvoiceUpdate.title: InvoiceUpdate

LeadUpdate.description:
A full replace of the editable fields — the edit form submits every
field together (same as AgencyClientUpdate).
LeadUpdate.title: LeadUpdate

MyWorkRead.description:
The signed-in member's assigned, not-done tasks across every project in
the agency — the data behind the dashboard's My Work tab.
MyWorkRead.title: MyWorkRead

PortalAgencyRead.description: The agency, as a client sees it — name + branding only, nothing internal.
PortalAgencyRead.title: PortalAgencyRead

PortalContextRead.description:
Everything the portal shell needs on load: the active membership plus
the full list (for a future switcher — the skeleton renders the first).
PortalContextRead.title: PortalContextRead

PortalMembershipRead.description: One (agency, client) the signed-in user is a portal contact for.
PortalMembershipRead.title: PortalMembershipRead

ProjectMemberRoleAssign.description: None clears the member's custom role label.
ProjectMemberRoleAssign.title: ProjectMemberRoleAssign

QualificationsUpdate.description:
Full replace of all three together — the qualifications form always
submits its whole state at once, same as NotificationSettingsUpdate.
QualificationsUpdate.title: QualificationsUpdate

TaskListMove.description: Just the position a drag interaction changes — mirrors TaskMove.
TaskListMove.title: TaskListMove

TaskListWithTasksRead.description: One kanban column plus its cards, already in display order — what GET .../board returns.
TaskListWithTasksRead.title: TaskListWithTasksRead

TaskMove.description: Just the fields a drag/quick-move interaction changes — lighter than a full TaskUpdate.
TaskMove.title: TaskMove

TaskTagsUpdate.description: Full replace of a task's tags — the tag picker always submits the complete set.
TaskTagsUpdate.title: TaskTagsUpdate

UnreadSummaryRead.description:
Total unread messages across all the caller's conversations in an
agency — what the top-nav badge shows.
UnreadSummaryRead.title: UnreadSummaryRead

UserProfileRead.description:
Photos + qualifications for the current user's own /profile pages.
Storage paths are never exposed — the frontend fetches the bytes through
GET /users/me/avatar (proxied), same convention as AgencyProfileRead.
UserProfileRead.title: UserProfileRead

WsTicketResponse.description:

see core/security.py's create_ws_ticket.
WsTicketResponse.title: WsTicketResponse

post.description:
Same request as ``POST .../messages``, but the reply streams in as
Server-Sent Events instead of arriving all at once. Once streaming
starts the HTTP status/headers are already sent, so an error mid-stream
can't become an HTTP error response — it's relayed as an in-band
``{"type": "error"}`` event instead, and the generator ends there
(no ``done`` event follows an ``error``).

get.description:
``?stripe=return`` (set by the onboarding return_url) triggers one live
reconciliation call if the row still looks pending — closes the race
between the redirect landing back and the v2.core.account.updated event
destination's webhook.

post.description:
Starts a real Stripe Checkout Session on the agency's own connected
account and returns the URL to redirect to. A deliberate break from the
old stub's "returns the paid invoice" contract — a hosted-Checkout
redirect can't be synchronous. The payment itself is recorded by the
Connect webhook once Stripe confirms it (see invoicing/webhooks_router.py).
